summary: This project is addressing the fact that young people do not understand the risks and requirements needed to manage and fly a space mission. We, TheHonoredVybe, have come up with a solution. We have vibe-coded a game that shows the exact requirements for operating a successful mission. From making the rocket in a budget, fixing problems like leaks on the USSS (US Space Station), and even landing a lunar command module on the moon, we have showed risks, stats, and a realistic mission to successfully complete the main objective. This game will spark curiosity in this field that most people do not understand!
details:
We made a game that uses realistic physics and real world situations of planning, making, flying, exploring, and experimenting on a space mission. At first, we have 2 possible ways that we can go: Exploring or Experimenting. Exploring is on the lunar module Eagle, where you have to successfully land a module on the moon. Experimenting is aboard the USSS, a fictional space station where you have to complete certain experiments in microgravity.

We used a vibe-coding agent called instaplay.ai, where we give prompts, and it codes.

We used canva to develop the project report slides.

Our project is creative as it showcases the exact fundamental details of planning an entire space mission, which is more scientific than player-pleasing.

We considered a variety of factors, such as electrical failures, cabin pressure, and cabin leaks that can change the way how smoothly a mission runs. At the beginning, when we are planning the rocket, we considered the budget of money we have, the mass, and the electricity needed on board in order to make this mission have no faults. We can add food packs water packs, electricity, and other lab equipment.
